# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)
- **CG-0MPD5XALT007F1WV** – Gym Graphics: Card Flip Animation (DeckRng + HandPile) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: 0mtorj5fs006b0un, acceptance, add, alias, apache (+136 more)
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — matched: acceptance, add, approach, art, asserts (+107 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: acceptance, add, alias, apache, approach (+104 more)

# Add per-turn running costs to Playground, Town Fountain and Community Shelter

## Summary

Give the three remaining free-to-run Main Street community-space cards a per-turn running cost, following the Park precedent (CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK) and the producer decision of 2026-09-29. Today the Playground (`cs-playground`), Town Fountain (`cs-fountain`) and Community Shelter (`cs-shelter`) have `ongoingCost` empty → 0, so they are free synergy/reputation anchors.

## Problem statement

The Park was given a 40 coins/turn running cost to stop costless synergy spam. Three other community spaces still have no ongoing cost, so the same "free anchor" dynamic remains for their synergies:

- **Playground** (`cs-playground`) — cost 400, Entertainment, +5 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Town Fountain** (`cs-fountain`) — cost 500, Culture, +10 rep/turn, ongoing 0.
- **Community Shelter** (`cs-shelter`) — cost 600, Service, +15 rep/turn, ongoing 0 (retiered T6→T3, CG-0MT5VZJLS000B8KI).

## Users

- **Player** — building a Playground/Fountain/Shelter cluster should feel the per-turn drain as a real strategic cost.
- **Producer / balance owner** — wants a running-cost lever on every community space, not just Park/Library/Garden/Kiosk/Public Art.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Card data** — `cs-playground`, `cs-fountain` and `cs-shelter` in the Main Street `card-data.csv` each have a non-zero integer `ongoingCost`, confirmed with the producer before merge. **Proposed mapping (agent suggestion, producer-owned — confirm or override): Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30.**
2. **Descriptions** — each updated `card-data.csv` description states the running cost using the existing wording ("Costs N coins per turn to run."), consistent with Library/Community Garden/Park, and the `card-text-data-consistency` test passes.
3. **Deduction** — at end of turn each placed, unsold card deducts its `ongoingCost` through the existing `applyCommunitySpaceOngoingCosts()` path, clamped at 0 coins and logged with an insufficient-funds log when applicable.
4. **Tooltips** — each card's community-space tooltip shows `Ongoing cost: -N/turn`; each card's cash line shows `-N`.
5. **Sold-card exemption preserved** — a sold Playground/Fountain/Shelter incurs no ongoing cost (CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA).
6. **Tests** — add distinct coverage for each card's deduction, clamping and sold-exemption (no redundant duplicates); update every test that assumes these cards are free to run, specifically:
   - `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — "does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards" uses Playground + Fountain + Shelter; re-point at cards that remain free, or rework with synthetic zero-cost card fixtures.
   - `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — "should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost" places a Playground; rework with a synthetic zero-cost community-space fixture.
   - `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` — "community space card with zero ongoingCost shows \"Ongoing cost: -0/turn\"" selects `find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`; after this change **no shipped community space has a zero `ongoingCost`**, so it must use a synthetic zero-cost card (business/staff variants already exist).
7. **Balance sanity** — Monte Carlo and tutorial guardrails remain green; any drift is measured and reported, and no guardrail band is silently widened. The tutorial scenario places no Playground/Fountain/Shelter (verified: tutorial uses Laundromat, Local Festival, Bookshop and Library only).
8. **Docs** — update `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (Ongoing/turn column), `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` (special-cases) and any other doc listing these cards' running costs.
9. **Full project test suite passes.**

## Constraints

- **Integer economy (hard):** coins are whole integers (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6); no fractional `ongoingCost`.
- **Data is source of truth:** the running cost lives in `card-data.csv`; tooltip, overlay and deduction derive from it.
- **Charging semantics unchanged:** placed, unsold cards only; clamped at 0; reuse the existing community-space mechanism.
- **Balance values are producer-owned:** the proposed mapping is an agent suggestion; the producer confirms or overrides before merge.
- **Zero-cost coverage must be synthetic:** after this change all eight shipped community spaces carry a non-zero `ongoingCost`, so tests of the "no ongoing cost" path can no longer rely on a shipped card.

## Existing state

- `cs-playground`: cost 400, baseIncome 0, Entertainment, rep 5, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-fountain`: cost 500, baseIncome 0, Culture, rep 10, `ongoingCost` empty.
- `cs-shelter`: cost 600, baseIncome 0, Service, rep 15, `ongoingCost` empty.
- Other community spaces already charged: Park 40, Library 25, Community Garden 10, Health Kiosk 15, Public Art 25.
- Park precedent: commit `5ffd54a` in `tce-main-street` set `cs-park` to 40/turn and updated tests/tooltip/cash-line/docs.
- Tests that assume these cards are free: `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` ("does not deduct for zero-ongoing-cost cards"); `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` ("should do nothing when no community space has an ongoing cost"); `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts` (`find(c => c.ongoingCost === 0)`).

## Key files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — set the three `ongoingCost` values and descriptions.
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerated by the suite; no SVG face change expected (community-space ongoing cost is not baked in).
- `tests/main-street/community-space-ongoing-cost.test.ts` — add per-card deduction/clamp/sold coverage; rework the Playground zero-cost test.
- `tests/main-street/community-space-tooltip.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/ongoing-cost-tooltips.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — tooltip/cash-line coverage; rework zero-cost selection.
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts` — rework the zero-cost test.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`, `balancing-methodology.md`.

## Related work

- **CG-0MU9NW9EP003B1AK** — Park running cost 40/turn (precedent; producer confirmed the integer-economy mapping).
- CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6 — integer economy ×100 rescale.
- CG-0MU3VH7QW006A2XA — sold cards excluded from ongoing costs.
- CG-0MRXYGM9B006I3PE — community-space ongoing-cost / Park-model synergy.
- CG-0MSQJ210I00491ZZ — Group B community-space expansion (added these three cards).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Value assumption:** the three proposed values (20/25/30) are an agent suggestion; the producer must confirm or override before merge.
- **Balance drift:** these cards appear in Monte Carlo simulations; run the guardrails and report drift rather than widening bands.
- **Test coupling:** three existing tests rely on these exact cards (or on any zero-cost community space) being free; all must be updated/reworked (expected, not a regression). After the change no shipped community space has `ongoingCost === 0`.
- **Scope creep:** additional community-space levers (e.g. adjusting Park/Library values) are out of scope; record them as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q (OPEN QUESTION):** The proposed `ongoingCost` values are Playground 20, Town Fountain 25, Community Shelter 30 (agent suggestion). Confirm these, or provide override values? — **Recommended:** accept 20 / 25 / 30 — it establishes a rising `ongoingCost` gradient (20/25/30) across the three cards while keeping them below the existing Park (40) and in the same band as Library (25) / Public Art (25). Answer: (pending producer). Source: producer decision required before merge (AC1); values are producer-owned balance data.
- **Q:** Are the three cards a single item or separate? — **Recommended:** single item — the change is one uniform data/description/edit sweep across three cards, sharing tests, docs and a single producer value decision. Answer: (agent, from seed context) single item. Source: work-item seed context.

## Summary

Main Street side of the Steam follow-to-unlock feature (core CG-0MSMAJQQT004SDCC, F5). Adds a "Follow us on Steam" call-to-action to the tutorial's final completion step (T26):

- `UnifiedTutorialStepDef.showSteamFollowCta` opt-in flag (T26 set).
- `MainStreetTutorialHints` renders the CTA in the completion tooltip: it opens the Steam store/community page through the launcher bridge (`window.tce.steamFollow`) when present, falls back to the web store page in a plain browser, and re-checks the follow (auto-detection, or the manual self-attest claim when the Steamworks binding has no `ISteamFriends::IsFollowing`).
- The CTA is additive — the existing "Let's play!" button still finishes the tutorial; following is never required (graceful degradation).
- Copy added to `tutorial-en.csv` (`tutorial.steamFollow.*`), keeping the CSV integrity contract green.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The tutorial's final step shows the Steam follow CTA (SLL-independent: it lives in the existing completion tooltip).

# Intake Brief: MainStreetNewGame restart selector test — reproduce and harden

**Work item:** MS-0MV2DNOCG0016INS · `bug` · `critical`
**Reported failure:** `tests/main-street/MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts > New Game overlay (browser) > presents the selector again after a scene restart (Play Again)`
**Reported symptom:** Timed out waiting for the scene restart / boot modal.
**Current reproducibility:** **Not reproduced on current `dev` HEAD (`53dfa69`).**

## Headline

A browser-suite run on 2026-10-10 12:35 UTC reported the "Play Again" restart test
timing out. On the current `dev` HEAD the test passes consistently in isolation
(3 runs × 2 tests) and in a full `--project browser` run (16:26 UTC), so the
failure is non-deterministic rather than a standing regression. The same full run
shows a sibling boot-ordering test failing with the signature of shared
origin-scoped state, so the fragility is real and should be pinned down before the
item is closed.

## Problem statement

The reported failure could not be reproduced. Either the test is flaky (an
order-dependent shared-state or timing race that only manifests under some suite
runs), or the original failing run was against a different tree state. Because
the failure is in the boot-modal/restart path, where multiple async layers and an
origin-scoped IndexedDB `SaveLoadStore` are involved, a flaky failure here can
mask a genuine product race or silently erode confidence in the browser suite.

## Users

- **Test maintainer / CI owner** — needs the browser suite to be deterministic so a
  red run means a real defect.
- **Developer** — needs a reproducible failing case (or a documented
  non-reproducibility decision) before spending implementation effort.
- **Player** — indirectly: a restart ("Play Again") must reliably re-present the
  New Game selector rather than resuming stale state (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP).

User story: *As a test maintainer, I want the restart selection browser test to be
deterministic and isolated from other test files' persisted state, so that a
failure always indicates a real defect.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Reproduce or rule out.** Run `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts` at least 10 times and the full `npx vitest run --project browser` suite at least twice on current `dev` HEAD. Record for each run whether the restart test passes. If it fails in any run, capture the failure output and the exact ordering/condition. Evidence (commands + outcomes) is recorded on the work item.
- **AC2 — Root cause.** Identify and document the mechanism by which the restart test can time out — e.g. a leftover IndexedDB `SaveLoadStore` run checkpoint being resumed after `scene.restart()` instead of the New Game selector, or an async boot/`restart()` race — with a code-level explanation.
- **AC3 — Deterministic regression test.** If a real defect exists, add a test that fails deterministically against the un-fixed behaviour and passes after the fix. If no defect exists, add a guard that deterministically pins the failure mode (e.g. boot with a seeded stale checkpoint and assert the selector-vs-resume outcome) so a future regression is caught.
- **AC4 — Browser-test isolation.** Browser tests that boot `MainStreetScene` start from clean origin-scoped state: the `SaveLoadStore` (run checkpoint **and** campaign progress) is cleared **before boot**, not only in `afterEach`, so one file cannot suppress another file's boot modal. This is demonstrated by a clean full-suite run.
- **AC5 — Behaviour preserved.** A scene restart ("Play Again") still resets `newGameSelectionMade` and re-presents the New Game selector when no run is being resumed; `resetNewGameSelectionFlag` retains its unit coverage. The tutorial-offer-first ordering (MS-0MV0319OC002H15F) is not weakened.
- **AC6 — Testing and validation.** New/updated tests fail against the pre-change code and pass after the change; `npm test` (unit) and the full `--project browser` suite pass.
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No product behaviour change unless a genuine defect is proven.** If the outcome is "not reproducible / already fixed", the deliverable is documented evidence plus test isolation hardening, not a speculative product edit.
- **Preserve the restart contract:** `newGameSelectionMade` is reset in `create()` so "Play Again" offers the selector again (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP).
- **Preserve boot-modal ordering:** tutorial offer first, then the New Game selector on skip/ineligible (MS-0MV0319OC002H15F).
- **Browser tests share the browser origin.** Vitest runs with `fileParallelism: false`, `sequence.concurrent: false` and `isolate: true`, but IndexedDB is origin-scoped and persists across test files; `localStorage` is likewise shared.
- **UK English** in all comments, docs and test names. No `CHANGELOG.md` edits (ship/release pipeline owns it).

## Existing state

- The test was introduced by `3ea7d07` (MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP) and extended by `0ceada0` (MS-0MV031A0B0026UL2) with `markTutorialSeen()` and an `afterEach` `clearSaveStore()` — an explicit defence against origin-shared IndexedDB leaking a checkpoint into a later file.
- The boot flow is layered and partly asynchronous:
  - `createScene()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) creates `newGameOverlay`, resets `newGameSelectionMade` via `resetNewGameSelectionFlag(s)`, and calls `loadCampaignAndSetup()`.
  - `loadCampaignAndSetup()` (`src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts`) loads campaign progress and then calls `checkForSavedCheckpoint()`.
  - `checkForSavedCheckpoint()` calls `checkpointManager.checkAndResume(...)`; **no** checkpoint → `showTutorialOfferOrDeferredBanner()` → `showNewGameSelector()`; **checkpoint** → resume overlay (selector never shown).
- Evidence on current `dev` HEAD `53dfa69`:
  - Isolated: `MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts` 2/2 pass, 3 consecutive runs (~15:09–15:15 UTC).
  - Full `--project browser`: `MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts` 2/2 pass; suite `4 failed | 71 passed (75)` at 16:26 UTC.
  - In the same full run, the sibling `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-ordering.browser.test.ts` failed with `Timed out waiting for tutorial offer modal visible after 5000ms` — a test that clears `localStorage` before boot but **not** the IndexedDB `SaveLoadStore`. This is consistent with a leftover checkpoint/campaign state from earlier tutorial e2e files suppressing the boot modal.

## Desired change

1. Reproduce the reported restart failure or establish, with recorded evidence, that it no longer occurs on `dev`.
2. If reproducible, fix the underlying cause (product race or state leakage).
3. Regardless of outcome, remove the shared-state fragility: browser boot tests clear the origin-scoped `SaveLoadStore` before booting, and the failure mode is pinned by a deterministic regression test.
4. Resolve the sibling `tutorial-offer-ordering` full-suite failure if it shares the same root cause.

**Open question (see Appendix):** whether to (a) close this item as no-longer-reproducible, (b) keep it open as a determinism/isolation hardening task, or (c) first recover the original failing run's log.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `tests/main-street/MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts` — the reported failing test; add pre-boot isolation and (if needed) the deterministic regression case.
- `tests/main-street/tutorial-offer-ordering.browser.test.ts` — sibling boot-ordering test failing in the full suite with the same shared-state signature.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetNewGameOverlay.ts` — `resetNewGameSelectionFlag`, overlay visibility.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — `createScene` reset + overlay creation + checkpoint wiring.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerTutorial.ts` — `showNewGameSelector` guard/flag handling.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign.ts` — `loadCampaignAndSetup` / `checkForSavedCheckpoint` async boot path.
- `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — canonical `CheckpointManager` / `SaveLoadStore` used by tests and scene.

## Related work

- **MS-0MUTTVR5K002ZDUP** — Playable AI competitive mode (epic). Introduced the restart regression coverage and the `resetNewGameSelectionFlag` helper.
- **MS-0MUTU8INS009MRR1** — Game-mode selector UI. Owns `MainStreetNewGameOverlay` and the boot-time selector.
- **MS-0MV031A0B0026UL2** — Browser modal-ordering and banner-timing tests. Added `tutorial-offer-ordering.browser.test.ts` and the `markTutorialSeen`/`clearSaveStore` defences to `MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts`.
- **MS-0MV0319OC002H15F** — Tutorial offer as the first blocking boot modal (ordering that must not regress).
- **MS-0MU14JDUG000E1V6** — Activity Log blank after scene restart (same `scene.restart()`/instance-reset family).
- **MS-0MUU24A3A005A7NW** — New Game overlay renders empty (same overlay).
- **MS-0MV1HALJ20003VK6** — Slot-bounds fix; the most recent `dev` commit (`53dfa69`) and the only tree change between the reported failure and the passing evidence.
- **MS-0MV2DORIC001Y9XZ**, **MS-0MV2DPSVB004B1WX** — sibling `[test-failure]` items created in the same batch; check for a common root cause.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **MS-0MTIILIBQ009J49F** – PRD M3 scope extension note; competitive unit tests; build verification (completed)
- **MS-0MUYK08I1004I19W** – Upgrade-deck composition lever: raise level-2 capstone reachability (market weight / copies) (completed)
- **MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ** – Rework pedestrians: road-walking and shop-entry reputation source (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: again, browser, dev, existing, failing, failure, play, pre, restart, scene, selector, suite, test, waiting
- `core/AGENTS.md` — matched: again, browser, dev, existing, failure, play, pre, restart, scene, selector, suite, test
- `core/CHANGELOG.md` — matched: again, browser, dev, existing, failing, failure, play, pre, scene, selector, suite, test

> The keyword matches above are low-precision (shared vocabulary); the manual **Related work** list is the authoritative set. Full report: `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-MS-0MV2DNOCG0016INS.md`.

## Assumptions

- The fetch/interpretation of the original 12:35 run is unavailable; the reported symptom is taken from the work-item description ("Timed out waiting for scene restart").
- "Deterministic" means the test outcome does not depend on which other browser test files ran earlier in the same suite.
- The `SaveLoadStore`/IndexedDB is the dominant cross-file state channel; `localStorage` tutorial state is already handled by `markTutorialSeen()`/`resetTutorialState()`.

## Risks

- **False "not reproducible" closure** — closing without at least N-run evidence could hide a real flake. *Mitigation:* AC1 mandates repeated isolated + full-suite runs with recorded evidence.
- **Scope creep into unrelated browser-test flakiness** — the full suite currently has other red tests (`upgrade-drag-drop`, `drag`, `HelpPanelLayering`, `tutorial-offer-ordering`). *Mitigation:* limit this item to the boot/restart selector path and the shared-state isolation it depends on; log unrelated reds as their own work items.
- **Weakening product behaviour** — clearing checkpoint state too aggressively could change resume semantics. *Mitigation:* isolate test-only state clearing; do not alter `CheckpointManager` product behaviour.
- **Flaky fix** — a timing increase (longer timeouts) would mask rather than fix. *Mitigation:* AC3 requires a deterministic regression test, not a timeout bump.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / disposition — OPEN QUESTION).** The reported failing test passes on current `dev` HEAD (`53dfa69`): 3 isolated runs and one full browser-suite run are green, while a sibling boot-ordering test fails in the full suite with the signature of shared origin-scoped IndexedDB state. How should this item proceed?
  - (a) **Close as no-longer-reproducible / already fixed** — record the evidence, make no code change. `Recommended` if the producer considers the 12:35 failure stale.
  - (b) **Keep open as a determinism/isolation hardening task** — fix the shared-state boot-test fragility (pre-boot `SaveLoadStore` clearing + deterministic regression test), including the sibling `tutorial-offer-ordering` failure if same-cause. `Recommended` — evidence shows a real, currently-red sibling with the same mechanism, so the hardening has demonstrable value even though the target test is currently green.
  - (c) **Investigate the original 12:35 run first** — recover its log/worktree before deciding; only then choose (a) or (b).
  - **Agent recommendation: (b)** — the sibling failure shows the shared-state mechanism is live today.
  - **Answer:** OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer.
  - **Evidence:** isolated runs `npx vitest run --project browser tests/main-street/MainStreetNewGame.browser.test.ts` (3× green, 15:09–15:15 UTC); full `npx vitest run --project browser` at 16:26 UTC (`MainStreetNewGame` green; `tutorial-offer-ordering` red with "Timed out waiting for tutorial offer modal visible after 5000ms"; suite 4 failed / 71 passed). Work-item description: "Browser suite failure (pre-existing on dev). Timed out waiting for scene restart."
